title: The straddle measures something else

title: The shape of what we don't believe

chapters.title: One volatility per option
chapters.dek: The model takes a single σ. The market refuses to supply one. Start by taking the refusal seriously.

chapters.title: The smile is a probability distribution
chapters.dek: Not analogous to one. Not a summary of one. The same object, and there is an exact formula that converts between them.

chapters.title: Two ways to make a smile
chapters.dek: Jumps and stochastic volatility both bend the surface. At a single expiry they are indistinguishable. Across expiries they are not.

chapters.title: The other axis
chapters.dek: A surface has two dimensions and most explanations only draw one. Term structure is where the tradeable information usually is.

chapters.dek: Black–Scholes delta assumes vol does not move when spot does. On a skewed surface that assumption is a choice, and it is worth real money.

title: Toolkit — vol to moves, vol cones, hedged P&L, Kelly sizing, vol drag

chapters.title: Turn a vol into a move before anyone finishes the sentence
chapters.dek: Annual vol over sixteen is a daily move. Everything else is the same square root.
figs: One-sigma move against horizon
Cheat sheet — one-sigma move as a percent of spot

chapters.title: Is this vol high? Only against its own history
chapters.dek: A vol cone puts today's realized vol at every lookback inside the range it has lived in. Implied gets judged against that, not against a feeling.
figs: Realized-vol cone

chapters.title: What a hedged option earns if your vol view is right
chapters.dek: Buy at implied, hedge daily, and the expected P&L is the gap between realized and implied variance , scaled by vega.
figs: Expected P&L of a long, delta-hedged ATM option, against realized vol

chapters.title: Having an edge is half of it; sizing is the other half
chapters.dek: An option bet with a positive expectation can still ruin you if it is too large. The Kelly fraction is the size that maximizes long-run growth.
figs: Long-run growth rate against the fraction bet

chapters.title: Volatility is a cost to anyone who compounds
chapters.dek: The median investor earns the average return minus half the variance. Lever it daily and the drag grows with the square of the leverage.
figs: Median wealth over time

title: Only one of them is tradeable

chapters.title: The square is not a detail
chapters.dek: A variance swap and a volatility swap on the same underlying, over the same window, do not have the same fair value. The gap is Jensen's inequality, and it is large.
figs: Realized volatility as a distribution, and the two fair strikes

chapters.title: One contract whose hedge pays exactly the variance
chapters.dek: Not approximately, and not on average. On every path, to five decimals.
figs: Hedged P&L against realized variance, one dot per path

chapters.title: Building it out of things that trade
chapters.dek: Nobody lists a log contract. You assemble one from ordinary options weighted by 1/K², and then never touch it again.
figs: The strip's payoff converging onto the log contract

chapters.title: The wings are not a detail either
chapters.dek: Cut the strike range to 92%–108% and a 25 variance swap prices at 17.4. The strikes nobody wants to quote are a third of the contract.

chapters.title: What the contract actually pays
chapters.dek: Quoted in volatility points, settled in variance, and convex in a direction that matters enormously to whoever is short.
figs: Payoff against realized volatility, and a linear vega position for comparison

chapters.dek: Not a forecast, not a sentiment gauge. A 30-day variance strip with a published rulebook.
